youtube.title: Why You Always Pick the Slow Queue #Shorts
youtube.description:
Maya picked the shortest queue. She still lost.

It isn't a curse, it's math: with three checkout lines, the chance that yours is the fastest is only 1 in 3 - two times out of three, another line wins, and the more checkouts there are, the worse your odds. One slow customer (a coupon, a price check, a card that won't work) freezes a whole line while the others keep moving. That's why some shops use one long "snake" line that feeds every till: a slow customer only blocks one till, and the line flows to the others.

Have you ever switched lines and instantly regretted it?

Sources:
- Why the other line always moves faster (probability): https://www.theblaze.com/news/2014/07/16/why-you-always-seem-to-get-stuck-in-the-slowest-line
- FlowingData on the 1-in-3 odds: https://flowingdata.com/?p=13484
- Bill Hammack (Engineer Guy) on queues and the single line: https://engineerguy.com/comm/4022.htm
- The most efficient checkout line: https://boingboing.net/2015/06/02/the-most-efficient-checkout-li.html

Maya, Sam and the shop are fictional.
